subject: microbiology
title: Nosocomial Infection, Device Bundles and Needle Stick Injury

steps.tx: **Nosocomial infection** (hospital acquired, healthcare associated) names infection neither present nor incubating at admission, conventionally appearing 48 hours or more after admission or within defined windows after discharge and procedures. The big four by device and site: catheter associated urinary infection, central line bloodstream infection, ventilator associated pneumonia and surgical site infection, each with bundle prevention and per thousand device days surveillance rates.
steps.say: Count infections per device days and prevention becomes a bundle, not a hope.

left.title: The big four
points: SSI: per hundred procedures by class

steps.tx: **Catheter bundles** work by subtraction and maintenance discipline: insert only for defined indications with sterile technique and closed drainage, keep bag below bladder without floor contact, review necessity daily and remove at the first honest opportunity (nurse led removal prompts), because every catheter day purchases biofilm time for uropathogens ascending inside and outside the lumen.
steps.say: The best catheter care is yesterday's removal decision.

nodes.label: Closed system, bag below bladder, securement

steps.tx: **Central line bundles** combine insertion maximal barrier precautions, chlorhexidine skin antisepsis, site selection avoiding femoral where possible, and maintenance (scrub the hub, dressing integrity, line necessity review), the Michigan Keystone programme having shown such bundles collapse bloodstream rates toward zero across whole states. Blood culture technique (paired sets, skin preparation, volume) decides whether CLABSI data mean anything.
steps.say: Scrub the hub, drape the patient, question the line daily: bundle steps are unglamorous and decisive.

left.title: Insertion bundle
points: Hand hygiene and maximal sterile barrier
Subclavian or jugular preference guided by risk

right.title: Maintenance bundle
points: Transparent dressing changed when damp or lifting

steps.tx: **Central line bundles** join several steps. Insertion uses maximal barrier precautions and chlorhexidine skin preparation, and avoids the femoral vein when another site is reasonable. Maintenance means scrubbing the hub, keeping the dressing intact, and reviewing every day whether the line is still needed. The Michigan Keystone programme showed such bundles can push bloodstream infection toward zero across whole states. Paired culture sets, skin preparation, and blood volume decide whether those data are true.
steps.say: A central line bundle uses full barrier precautions and chlorhexidine at insertion, prefers a site other than the femoral vein, then scrubs the hub, protects the dressing, and asks daily if the line is still needed. Keystone work in Michigan showed this can collapse line infections across a state. Culture technique and volume decide if the numbers are real.

vis.alt: A clinician inserts a central line using maximal barrier precautions, with full drape, cap, mask, sterile gown, and chlorhexidine on the skin.
vis.caption: Maximal barrier draping, chlorhexidine on the skin, and a preference for a site other than the femoral vein are shown as a central line is inserted. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Ventilator bundles** elevate the head end 30 to 45 degrees, wake and breathe patients daily (sedation interruption with spontaneous breathing trials), give peptic ulcer and thrombosis prophylaxis by risk, oral chlorhexidine traditions (now debated by outcome data), and subglottic suction endotracheal tubes in selected units, each element arguing that pneumonia prevention is positioning and liberation, not antibiotics.
steps.say: Raise the bed, wake the patient, trial the breath: pneumonia prevention is posture and liberation.

left.title: Bundle elements
points: Daily sedation interruption and breathing trial

steps.tx: **Surgical site infection** prevention spans the perioperative arc: preoperative bathing, clipping not shaving, antibiotic prophylaxis within the hour before incision and stopped within a day, glycaemic and temperature control, oxygenation debates, and wound class stratification (clean to dirty) that makes rates comparable. Organisms mirror the incision's neighbourhood: staphylococci for skin, enterics for bowel.
steps.say: Prophylaxis timed to the incision hour and stopped by tomorrow is SSI prevention's antibiotic sentence.

left.title: Prevention arc
points: Clip, do not shave; bath preoperatively

right.title: SSI grammar
points: Superficial, deep and organ space classes
Wound classes clean to dirty stratify risk

steps.tx: **Needle stick injury** management runs on minutes and serology: wash immediately (no squeezing rituals or bleach), report and document, source patient tested with consent for HIV, hepatitis B and C, exposed worker's hepatitis B immunity verified, HIV post exposure prophylaxis within 72 hours (ideally under 2, three drug 28 days), hepatitis B immunoglobulin by immunity status, and follow up testing scheduled before the worker leaves the department.
steps.say: Wash, report, test the source, start PEP inside 72 hours; the clock is the protocol.

nodes.label: Wash wound, flush mucosae, no bleach
HIV PEP within 72 hours, HBV by immunity
Follow up serology and adherence support

steps.tx: **Needle stick injury** care runs on minutes and on serology. Wash the wound at once. Do not squeeze it and do not use bleach. Report and document the event. Test the source, with consent, for HIV, hepatitis B, and hepatitis C. Check the worker hepatitis B immunity. HIV post exposure prophylaxis is a three drug course for 28 days, begun inside 72 hours and ideally inside 2. Hepatitis B immunoglobulin follows immune status. Book follow up tests before the worker leaves.
steps.say: Wash a needle stick at once, without squeezing or bleach, then report it. Test the source, with consent, for HIV and hepatitis B and C, and check the worker hepatitis B immunity. Start three drug HIV prophylaxis within 72 hours, ideally within 2, for 28 days. Hepatitis B immunoglobulin depends on immunity. Arrange follow up before leaving.

vis.alt: A flowchart traces needle stick care from immediate washing through source testing, worker hepatitis B status, and the timing of HIV drugs.
vis.caption: The sequence runs from wound washing and reporting to source serology, the worker hepatitis B immunity, and a 72 hour limit for HIV post exposure drugs. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Transmission precautions** layer over standard precautions by syndrome: contact (gowns, gloves, dedicated equipment for MRSA, C difficile, Candida auris), droplet (surgical masks within two metres for influenza and meningococcus), airborne (fit tested respirators and negative pressure for tuberculosis, measles, varicella), prescribed empirically at triage before diagnoses confirm, because waiting for certainty infects the waiting room.
steps.say: Isolate by syndrome at the door; confirmation refines, never initiates, precautions.

left.title: Precaution tiers
points: Contact: gown gloves, single room priority

right.title: Empiric triggers
points: Cough with TB risk: airborne immediately

steps.tx: **Infection control structure** (hospital infection control committee, infection control nurses per beds, microbiology laboratory partnership, antimicrobial stewardship sibling from the pharmacology lessons) owns surveillance, outbreak investigation (line lists, epidemic curves, molecular typing), policy and audit. Outbreaks are declared on data, investigated by hypothesis and ended by sustained zero, not by optimism.
steps.say: Line list, epidemic curve, hypothesis, intervention: outbreaks end on sustained data.

left.title: Outbreak method
points: Environmental and staff sampling by hypothesis
